chunks: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, from his father عليه السلام, that 'Ali عليه السلام used to say:

There is no amputation upon anyone who has been intimidated by beating, restraint, imprisonment, or harsh treatment, unless he confesses. If he confesses, his hand is amputated; and if he does not confess, it is dropped from him on account of the intimidation.

key_terms.تُخُوِّفَ: to be intimidated or put in fear through coercive pressure
key_terms.قَطْعَ: amputation as the prescribed hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.يَعْتَرِفَ: to confess or admit the offense
key_terms.ٱلتَّخْوِيفِ: intimidation or threat that affects legal responsibility

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd punishment for theft apply when a confession is obtained under threat or intimidation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the hadd of theft when an accused person is subjected to intimidation or coercive pressure. It indicates that threatened or coercive circumstances affect the legal standing of the case, and it treats confession under such conditions as central to the enforcement of the punishment.
